newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares forge ahead on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares forge ahead on bullish sentiment.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares continued their march ahead on Friday on bullish investor sentiment bolstered by falling interest rates and expectations of normal rains.

The key industrial index soared 116.76 points -- a 1.6 percent rise -- breaking through the psychological 7,600-mark to end at a new all time peak of 7,616.42. This was a leap of 259.55 points on the week.

"The market is just strong, strong, strong. It's being driven by sentiment. We are expecting a good rainy season, interest rates are coming down. There's no real bad news. It's very positive," one broker said.
On Friday, Zimbabwe's hotels and supermarkets group Meikles Africa started trading on the bourse in reasonable volume at 1,600 cents compared to its international offer price of 1,400 cents.

The group's offering is the largest equity offering ever to be undertaken by a Zimbabwe-based firm and it follows a reverse takeover of cash shell Northchart Investments Ltd, giving Meikles a primary listing on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) and a secondary one in London.

Among the winners on the ZSE on Friday, horticulture firm Ariston rose 50 cents to 1,600, soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes climbed 40 cents to 740 while tyre producer Dunlop and winery Afdis each gained 20 cents to 210 and 475 respectively.
Transport group Clan at 260, sugar-cane grower Hippo at 870, tea company Tanganda at 265 and packaging firm Hunyani at 370 all added 10 cents.
The only losers were food canning firm Natfoods, clothing and furniture retailer Tedco and cement producer Porthold which all shed 10 cents to 660, 450 and 1,280 respectively.
In minings, trading was active and firm with five cent gains in copper company MCM at 25 and Wankie Colliery at 360 in reasonable turnover.

However, Falgold lost five cents to 140 following its relegation from the International Finance Corporation main index from November 1. It will be replaced by Wankie which dealers said was already popular with external investors.

Gold producer Ashanti dropped 100 cents to 14,000 on the back of an easier bullion price on international markets. The mining index shed 5.39 points to end at 1,248.77 -- a loss of 5.76 points on the week.
